title: NOAI WordPress Content & Media Export
description: Schema for a full export of noai.philosophers.group content, derived from live inspection of its WP REST API (wp-json/wp/v2) on 2026-09-18. All endpoints below were reachable unauthenticated (public read access); no login/application password required for GET. WP Posts and the category taxonomy are intentionally excluded from this export/schema - posts were deleted from the working dataset, and every category was migrated to an equivalent tag and dropped in favor of tags-only classification.

site_images.description: Favicon/social-share image pools, built by scripts/build-media-manifest.js from media/icon-*/media/ogg-* files. index.html picks one of each at random on every load.

icons.description: Relative media/ paths, favicon candidates (ideally square).

ogg.description: Relative media/ paths, social-share image candidates (ideally ~1200x630+).

renderedString.description: Standard WP 'rendered HTML + raw source (edit context only)' wrapper used for title/content/excerpt/guid.

pluginFields.description: Fields injected by installed plugins. Shape is plugin/post-defined and NOT fixed - treat as opaque/passthrough. Observed empty ([] or {}) on sampled items but may be populated on others (e.g. presentations with speaker/session details).

acf.description: Advanced Custom Fields data. Empty array when no fields configured for this post/type, otherwise an object of field_name -> value.

mb.description: Meta Box plugin fields. Same empty-array-vs-object behavior as acf.

mfb_rest_fields.description: List of field names the mfb plugin exposes for this item, e.g. ['title','yoast_head','yoast_head_json'].

meta.description: Registered post meta, e.g. {_acf_changed, inline_featured_image, ...}. Keys vary by post type/plugin config.

yoast_head.description: Pre-rendered <head> HTML block from Yoast SEO (title/meta/OG tags).

yoast_head_json.description: Structured equivalent of yoast_head - title, description, OG/Twitter card data, schema.org graph, etc.

linksBlock.description: HAL-style _links block; useful for discovering related resources (author, featured media, terms, revisions) without guessing IDs.

postCommon.description: Fields shared by page and presentations (all built on WP_Post).

featured_media.description: 0 = none. Non-zero = id resolvable via GET /wp/v2/media/{id}.

page.description: GET /wp-json/wp/v2/pages (38 items). Static pages; hierarchical via 'parent'.

presentation.description: GET /wp-json/wp/v2/presentations (101 items). Custom post type - festival sessions/talks. IMPORTANT: session/speaker details (date, time, location, presenter name/bio/photo) are stored as Meta Field Block (mfb) custom fields that are NOT exposed via the REST API (acf/mb/meta come back empty for every item checked - 10/10 samples). These fields ARE rendered on the live page and must be scraped from the rendered HTML at `link` instead - see scraped_fields below.

tags.description: Term IDs, resolve via tags[]. Includes migrated former-category tags, e.g. 'NOAI 2025 Presentation'.

scraped_fields.description: NOT part of the REST API response. Must be obtained by fetching the rendered page at `link` and parsing '.wp-block-mfb-meta-field-block' elements under the 'Presentation Details' (h3) and 'Presenter Biography' (h2) sections. See scrape_presentation.py.

presenter_name.description: Can be blank/missing on some items (observed on 1/10 samples) - layout may vary for panels vs. single speakers.

presenter_photo_url.description: Usually matches the post's featured_media image, but scraped directly as a fallback.

type.description: Session type (e.g. 'Workshop', 'Panel', 'Fireside Chat'), sourced from an external CSV schedule import, not the live site - may be an empty string for a plain talk slot where the schedule left this column blank.

source_url.description: Direct, downloadable file URL for this size variant.

media.description: GET /wp-json/wp/v2/media/{id} (296 items total). NOTE: the list endpoint (?per_page=N&page=M) was observed returning an empty [] for some pages despite correct x-wp-total/x-wp-totalpages headers, while single-item GETs by id worked reliably. A robust harvester should sweep ids 1..N (skipping 404s) and/or retry empty list pages, rather than trusting paginated listing alone.

source_url.description: Direct, downloadable URL for the full/original file - the main field needed to actually pull the asset.

post.description: ID of the post this attachment belongs to, or null if unattached.

scheduleItem.description: The published festival schedule, sourced from an organizer-provided CSV (not the WP site) - see scripts/build_schedule.py. Every session slot is included, even ones with no dedicated presentation page (meals, receptions, parties, opening/closing remarks) - this is the authoritative full schedule, presentations[] is the subset with a full write-up.

sort_time.description: 24h HH:MM start time for chronological sorting.

raw_time_range.description: Original CSV time range string, e.g. '2:05–2:35'.

presenters.description: Free-text presenter name(s) as published in the schedule, may differ slightly from presentation.scraped_fields.presenter_name.

type.description: e.g. 'Workshop', 'Panel', 'Fireside Chat', 'Party', 'Food', 'Informational'. Often blank for a plain talk slot.

tag.description: Single topic label as published, e.g. 'AI & Technology'. Not the same as presentation tags[].

presentation_id.description: Resolves via presentations[].id for full bio/description/photo. null when this slot has no dedicated presentation page.

term.description: GET /wp-json/wp/v2/tags. The category taxonomy was retired - every former category was migrated to an equivalent tag (matched by name, created if missing) and the category itself deleted, so tags is now the only classification collection. NOTE: 'count' as returned by the public REST API undercounts real usage since it excludes draft content - recompute actual usage from tags[] on pages/presentations rather than trusting this field at face value.

count.description: Number of items using this term - corrected here to reflect real usage (including drafts), not the raw REST API value.
